methods.name: signIn
methods.docs: Signs in, silently where the platform allows. Call once at launch; it never blocks play.

methods.name: isSignedIn
methods.docs: Whether a player is signed in right now, without trying to sign in.

methods.name: getServerProof
methods.docs: Proof of the signed-in player for your server. Fails if nobody is signed in.

methods.name: submitScore
methods.docs:
Posts a score to a leaderboard (your ID from App Store Connect or Play Console). Whole numbers only. Fails quietly
(resolves) when nobody is signed in, so games can call it without checking.

methods.name: unlockAchievement
methods.docs: Unlocks an achievement. Does nothing if it's already unlocked or nobody is signed in.

methods.name: setAchievementProgress
methods.docs:
Sets an achievement's progress, 0 to 100 percent. Android needs the achievement made "incremental" in Play Console
with 100 steps; iPhone takes the percentage directly. Progress never goes backwards.

methods.name: showLeaderboard
methods.docs: Shows the platform's own leaderboard screen: one board, or all of them.

methods.name: showAchievements
methods.docs: Shows the platform's own achievements screen.

properties.name: signedIn
properties.docs: Whether a player is signed in to the platform's games service now.

properties.name: reason
properties.docs:
Why not, when `signedIn` is false: `unavailable` (no games service here, e.g. the web), `declined` (the player
cancelled or turned it off), `restricted` (blocked by parental controls or the device), or `error`.

properties.name: message
properties.docs: Extra detail from the platform when something went wrong. Never shown to players as is.

properties.name: interactive
properties.docs:
Android only: show Google's sign-in screen if the silent sign-in didn't work. Leave false at launch (Play Games
signs in on its own when it can) and use true only from a button the player pressed. iPhone always shows Game
Center's own sheet the first time, as Apple requires.

properties.name: playerId
properties.docs: The team-scoped player ID (teamPlayerID). Only valid for one developer's games. Never display it.

properties.name: bundleId
properties.docs: The app's bundle ID, which the signature covers.

properties.name: publicKeyUrl
properties.docs: Where Apple's public key is. The server must only fetch it from Apple's own domain.

properties.name: timestamp
properties.docs: Milliseconds since 1970, as a string (it doesn't fit a JavaScript number safely in every case).

interfaces.name: PlayGamesProof
interfaces.docs: A one-time server auth code from Play Games (GamesSignInClient.requestServerSideAccess).

properties.name: authCode
properties.docs: Swap it on your server, once, for the player's ID. Expires within minutes.

properties.name: serverClientId
properties.docs:
Android: the OAuth client ID of your game's "Games server" credential in Play Console (a web client). Required on
Android, ignored on iPhone.

typeAliases.name: GamesPlatform
typeAliases.docs: Which games service the device uses. `none` on the web.

typeAliases.name: ServerProof
typeAliases.docs:
Proof of who the player is, for your own server to check (see `capacitor-game-services/server`). Never trust a
player ID the phone simply tells you.
